chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, in a hadith of his which he attributes to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Regarding the Mu'li (one who makes a vow of abstention from his wife), he must either return (to conjugal relations) or divorce her; if he does so, [the vow is fulfilled], and if not, his neck is struck (i.e., he is executed).

key_terms.الْمُؤْلِي: A man who makes a vow of Ila (abstention from his wife)
key_terms.ضُرِبَتْ عُنُقُهُ: His neck was struck (idiom for execution)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a husband who makes a vow of abstention from his wife and does not resume relations or divorce her?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific judicial consequence of prolonged 'Ila' (vow of abstention), distinguishing between the husband's voluntary choice to reconcile or divorce versus the mandatory penalty of execution if he remains inactive. While the Quranic verses establish the four-month waiting period, this hadith emphasizes the ultimate legal resolution in the Shia jurisprudential tradition, highlighting the seriousness of neglecting marital rights during this period.
